Task 2 independent spec and quality review - 2026-10-20
Disposition: Changes requested (3 Important findings; no Critical findings established).

Review basis and limits
- Reviewed current working source for V4__rag_assistance.sql, ai/** excluding model implementation review, AiIntegrationTest and AiResultValidatorTest, plus the G3 KnowledgeController job-route relocation.
- Read Global Constraints, Review Focus and Task2 in docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-20-g4-rag-assistance.md, the G4 design in docs/10-RAG设计与评测.md, and task-2-report.txt.
- Cross-scope reads were limited to the named caller/port input bounds, ticket/catalog validation limits, shared exception mapping, and G3 publication/ACL lock behavior. No product, Git, configuration, database or test mutations were performed. This report is the only written file.
- There is no HEAD/immutable reviewed commit. This is a review of the current working source; the staged G0-G2 and working G3/G4 tree was preserved. Findings identify exact current source lines, not an immutable diff.
- All findings below are static code-path findings, not newly executed runtime reproductions. No tests, builds, browser sessions, external model calls, dependency scans or broad source scans were run by this reviewer.
- Independently inspected existing root evidence .work/g4-backend-green.log: 25 integration + 5 validator + 1 evaluation = 31 tests, zero failures/errors/skips, BUILD SUCCESS. docs/evidence/g4-rag-evaluation.json records 32 mock cases (20 positive/12 refusal), recallAt5 1.0, candidate-label citation precision 1.0 and refusal error 0.0. These are existing root results, not reviewer-run checks or real-provider quality evidence.

Important 1 [P2]: Allocate caller context within the model-port bounds instead of rejecting valid tickets.
Primary location: backend/src/main/java/com/ticknova/ai/AiWorker.java:42-50,93-95.
Related: backend/src/main/java/com/ticknova/ai/AiRetriever.java:18-21; backend/src/main/java/com/ticknova/ai/model/AiText.java:58-65,70-84; backend/src/main/java/com/ticknova/ticket/TicketDtos.java:10.
The worker concatenates the complete title and description and embeds it for every draft kind. Ticket descriptions legally allow 20,000 characters, but both concrete adapters enforce 8,192 characters per embedding text. With at least one readable space and nonempty terms, a valid 9,000-character description deterministically causes AI_INPUT_TOO_LARGE and a terminal FAILED job before SUMMARY, CLASSIFICATION or REPLY can run. A readable space need not contain any usable evidence: embedding happens before SQL returns candidates. Ticket-only summary/classification therefore also fail solely because unrelated knowledge retrieval was attempted.
There is a related aggregate-budget failure: fixed reply/source budgets (12,000/24,000) and up to 200 service names are assembled independently; checkBudget then rejects totals above 60,000 rather than fitting context to the remaining budget. Legal short tickets with many long active service names and sufficient replies/sources can trigger this independently of the embedding-text limit. For example 200 names of 160 characters count as 39,200 including the worker's UUID allowance; 12,000 replies + 12,000 sources + a 1,000-character description already exceed the worker limit.
Recommendation: use an explicit bounded retrieval query; allocate generation context deterministically against the remaining port budget, retain useful ticket content and source identities, and avoid unnecessary retrieval for truly ticket-only operations. Keep both per-item and aggregate bounds enforced. The public-reply COUNT concern is already handled by AiAuthorization.java:41 LIMIT 100 and is not a separate finding.
Focused regression: use the concrete mock adapter or a contract-enforcing test double with 8,192 and 8,193 boundary queries and legal 20,000-character ticket descriptions across all draft kinds; include at least one readable space. Add one legal classification case with 200 long service names and populated context, asserting bounded supplied input and defined completion rather than terminal oversized-input failure. Do not solve this by raising the model limit without a budgeting policy.

Important 2 [P1]: Knowledge input provenance can disappear when summary/classification outputs omit citations.
Primary location: backend/src/main/java/com/ticknova/ai/AiWorker.java:43-53,78-82.
Related: backend/src/main/java/com/ticknova/ai/AiResultValidator.java:17-25; backend/src/main/java/com/ticknova/ai/AiService.java:75-77.
All draft kinds receive recalled knowledge chunks, while SUMMARY and CLASSIFICATION legitimately accept empty citationChunkIds. Completion and later reads/feedback revalidate only the citations returned by the model, and ai_citation persists only that same list. A valid SUMMARY output can copy content from a supplied chunk while returning [] citations; withdrawing/superseding that document during generation or after completion leaves the original space ACL valid, so the derived output is still persisted/returned. The source document has disappeared from the saved authorization dependencies. This violates Review Focus 1's source withdrawal guarantee even though the ordinary ANSWER-with-citation regression passes. The model must not be responsible for choosing which supplied private source dependencies survive authorization checks.
Recommendation: persist and revalidate the full set of actually supplied knowledge-source dependencies independently of user-visible/model-selected citations, or make ticket-only summary/classification truly ticket-only by excluding knowledge inputs. Merely requiring one citation would still leave other supplied sources untracked. The same full-input dependency policy should cover answered text when a model cites only a subset of supplied chunks.
Focused regression: a deterministic model stub receives a recalled chunk and returns its distinctive content in SUMMARY with no citation IDs. Withdraw that document once inside generation and once after completion. Assert no persisted/displayed derived body after invalidation, feedback is withheld, and audit occurs once. Add a multi-source ANSWER citing only one source, then withdraw the other supplied source, if full-input provenance is chosen. No real model call is needed.

Important 3 [P2]: Concurrent feedback/withholding can escape the documented API outcome as HTTP 500.
Primary location: backend/src/main/java/com/ticknova/ai/AiService.java:24,79-90.
Related: backend/src/main/java/com/ticknova/shared/ApiErrors.java:54-58 (generic exception handler).
The service uses REPEATABLE READ for both reads and feedback. Two concurrent feedback transactions can establish snapshots before either commits; the second SELECT ... FOR UPDATE waits for the first row update, then PostgreSQL can raise a serialization failure instead of reaching the same-feedback replay or different-feedback 409 branch. Concurrent job reads that both detect invalid sources similarly race on UPDATE ... AND NOT withheld. There is no bounded transaction retry or serialization-to-domain handling, so the exception reaches the generic 500 INTERNAL_ERROR handler. Existing tests cover sequential feedback replay/conflict and sequential withhold-audit-once only. No stale response disclosure was demonstrated; this finding is a predictable concurrency/API reliability defect.
Recommendation: retry the whole snapshot transaction a bounded number of times for serialization failures, preserving fresh authorization and atomic auditing; then produce the documented idempotent/conflict/source-unavailable outcome. Do not continue inside an aborted transaction or weaken source checks.
Focused regression: coordinate two transactions with barriers to overlap same-feedback requests (both 204, one audit), opposite-feedback requests (one 204, one 409), and two reads/feedbacks after withdrawal (stable SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, one withholding audit). Assert no generic 500 and audit rollback semantics remain intact.

Verified positive design observations (static review and existing tests)
- AiRetriever.java:30-54 materializes active actor/space/member/current publication/profile-ready sources before top-8 vector/FTS candidates and deterministic RRF top-6; values are bound, and ADMIN has no content bypass.
- Original effective spaces are persisted once; replay, work, completion, reads and feedback recheck the entire set. Empty readable sets and later membership expansion are explicitly covered.
- AI jobs are creator-only; active/must-change state is freshly checked. Ticket input selects PUBLIC_REPLY only, with no internal note or resolution-note input. Feedback records a choice without ticket mutation.
- Request/job/outbox/audit creation and result/outbox/audit completion share transactions. Row claims use SKIP LOCKED, lease tokens fence stale commits, attempts/backoff are finite, indexing resumes in bounded batches, and profile matching gates retrieval.
- Result validation rejects forged/duplicate citation IDs and invalid classification fields; refusal returns no unvalidated model body.
- V4 keeps embedding state separate from G3 ingest state and gives suggestions unique job linkage and citation foreign keys. Unified JobController delegates non-AI jobs to the unchanged KnowledgeService response path.
- The revised lexical gate is documented as >=30% terms and at least two matches (one for one-term queries); real-only cosine >=0.75 remains uncalibrated. Existing mock evaluation does not establish semantic paraphrase quality, human groundedness, classification Macro-F1 or P95.

No Minor findings added. Further broad checks remain root Task4 responsibilities. Re-review the concrete fixes and their focused regression evidence before accepting Task2.
